item.notes: Initial .cl-only proposal, no support claim. Membership is fixed by pool-rule.json using licence, whole-project pin, predeclared roles and the named hashcat structural exception. Hashcat's diagnostic role was assigned after its round-1 screen because computed includes and qualifier macros require a compiler-evidenced context; review accepted the exception. The historical inclusive pool would fail at 1,482/1,735 (85.42%). The seven previously screened OSI primary populations fail natively: dedicated 133/378 = 35.19%. PyOpenCL enters under that same rule before its screen. HandsOn CC-BY-3.0 is diagnostic-only and cannot calibrate under design §13.3 step 16. Preserve every .cl including fragments and duplicates in tenancy. Positive C/OpenCL sniff, Lisp/Cool negatives, ambiguous refusal, tier-B reconstructed CL3.0/SPIR64 context and shared active_lines filtering remain required. No L3/L4 claim. The full frozen eight-project pool now fails at 138/386 = 35.75%, including PyOpenCL at 5/8; none of those results changes membership. After G-R1 opened implementation, all five named native grammar candidates still fail admission. The patched candidate improves dedicated 138/386 to 63/386 with zero regressions/faults. The separate pre-tuning holdout improves 25/53 to 2/53 and never enters the primary gate. No language level is claimed. G-R6 bars the requested clBLAS prepass because the other 23 failures alone exceed the maximum 19/386.
